intent.raw_query: Patagonia hiking Torres del Paine, $4500, 12 days, December 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Torres del Paine, Patagonia

experiences.name: W Trek Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic W Trek, a 4-5 day trekking route through Torres del Paine National Park covering the Valle del Francés, Grey Glacier, and the iconic Torres viewpoint. Experience dramatic landscapes of granite towers, turquoise lakes, and Patagonian steppe with overnight stays in mountain refugios or campsites.
experiences.location: Torres del Paine National Park, Central Circuit

experiences.name: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Trek the challenging 8-hour round-trip trail to the base of the iconic Torres del Paine granite towers. Start before dawn to witness the legendary alpenglow phenomenon where the towers glow fiery orange and pink at sunrise, reflecting in the glacial lake below. One of Patagonia's most breathtaking natural spectacles.
experiences.location: Mirador Base Las Torres, Eastern Sector

experiences.name: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition
experiences.description: Paddle through iceberg-dotted waters of Lago Grey alongside the massive Grey Glacier, one of Patagonia's most accessible glaciers. A guided kayaking experience allows you to get up close to towering blue ice walls and floating icebergs while surrounded by the raw wilderness of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field.

experiences.name: Valle del Francés Trekking Day
experiences.description: Hike through the spectacular Valle del Francés, a glacially carved valley flanked by hanging glaciers, waterfalls, and the dramatic Cuernos del Paine peaks. Ascend to the Mirador Británico viewpoint for a 360-degree panorama of the park's most stunning peaks and valleys. Watch for condors soaring overhead.

experiences.name: Patagonian Wildlife and Pampas Nature Walk
experiences.description: Explore the open Patagonian steppe and lakeside trails around Lago Sarmiento and Laguna Amarga to spot abundant wildlife including guanacos, rheas, Andean condors, flamingos, and pumas in their natural habitat. A guided nature walk reveals the unique flora and fauna of the Patagonian ecosystem beyond the main trekking routes.
experiences.location: Laguna Amarga and Lago Sarmiento, Northern Entrance Sector

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Torres del Paine, Patagonia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 22:30. Arrange pre-booked budget shuttle or shared transfer to accommodation near Torres del Paine. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your Beachfront room. Grab a light snack from any 24-hour convenience store or hotel reception if available.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport café
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport café
meals.dinner: Pack a sandwich or snack from airport kiosk — budget ~$5–8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your shuttle transfer in advance to save money. Shared shuttles from Puerto Natales to Torres del Paine run ~$15–25 USD per person. Keep tomorrow free for rest — do not over-schedule after a late arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a slow start, enjoy a budget breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café. Visit the local park entrance information center to purchase your Torres del Paine National Park entry pass (~$35 USD for international visitors in high season) and pick up free trail maps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely orientation walk around the hotel's beachfront area and nearby lakeshore. Familiarize yourself with the landscape, spot local Patagonian wildlife such as guanacos, Andean condors, and flamingos near the water. Visit the nearest ranger station to ask about current trail conditions and weather forecasts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel. Organize and pack your gear for the upcoming multi-day hikes. Check and repack your daypack with essentials: water, snacks, layers, rain gear. Head to a local budget restaurant in Puerto Natales or the hotel dining area for a hearty early dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local café — budget menu del día ~$6–10 USD
meals.lunch: Self-prepared sandwiches and fruit from a local grocery store — ~$4–6 USD
meals.dinner: Budget restaurant in Puerto Natales — try a set menu (menú del día) with soup, main, and drink for ~$10–14 USD

day_by_day.notes: Buy your national park pass early — lines can be long in December (peak season). Stock up on trail snacks, energy bars, and instant meals at a supermarket in Puerto Natales today to save significantly over the next 12 days.

day_by_day.morning: Early start at 05:30. Pack a hearty breakfast and take the shared shuttle or park bus to the Mirador Las Torres trailhead at the Hostería Las Torres area. Begin the iconic 8-hour round-trip Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike. The trail climbs through lenga beech forest, open rocky terrain, and a steep final moraine ascent to reach the base of the three granite towers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach the mirador at the base of the towers — a glacial turquoise lake surrounded by the dramatic granite spires. Spend 30–45 minutes taking in the views, eating your packed lunch, and photographing the landscape. Begin the descent back down the moraine and through the forest toward the trailhead.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the trailhead by approximately 16:00–17:00. Catch the return shuttle or park bus back to the hotel. Shower, rest, and tend to any blisters or sore muscles. Enjoy a well-earned hearty dinner.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared oats or bread with peanut butter — packed from grocery supplies — ~$2–3 USD
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch: sandwiches, nuts, energy bars, fruit — ~$4–5 USD
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant or nearby budget eatery — lamb stew or pasta — ~$12–15 USD

day_by_day.notes: This is the most popular hike in the park — start as early as possible to beat crowds and afternoon wind. Wear waterproof layers as Patagonian weather can change rapidly. The total elevation gain is approximately 800m. Trekking poles are highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Active rest day. Sleep until 07:30. Enjoy a slow breakfast. Take a short and gentle 2–3 hour lakeside walk along Lago del Toro or the nearest accessible shoreline from the hotel. Birdwatch for black-necked swans, upland geese, and steamer ducks. Bring binoculars if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Salto Grande waterfall, one of the most accessible and dramatic viewpoints in the park — reachable by park bus or shared taxi. The powerful waterfall connects Lago Nordenskjöld with Lago Pehoé. Walk the short 1km loop trail around the viewpoint. Spot guanacos grazing on the hillsides.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel by 17:00. Prepare and cook a budget meal using groceries purchased in Puerto Natales — pasta with canned tomato sauce and tuna is a classic trekker's meal. Plan and review gear for the upcoming Valle del Francés hike.

meals.breakfast: Instant oatmeal with dried fruit and instant coffee — ~$2 USD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Salto Grande viewpoint — crackers, cheese, salami, fruit — ~$4 USD
meals.dinner: Self-cooked pasta with canned tuna and tomato sauce in hotel room or communal kitchen — ~$3–4 USD

day_by_day.notes: Check if your accommodation has a communal kitchen — many budget-friendly spots in Patagonia do. Self-cooking saves $8–15 per meal. Salto Grande is free to visit with your park pass already purchased.

day_by_day.morning: Early start at 06:00. Take the park bus or catamaran ferry across Lago Pehoé to reach the Valle del Francés trailhead at Campamento Italiano. Begin the Valle del Francés Trekking Day — a full-day hike through a glacially carved valley flanked by hanging glaciers, dramatic waterfalls, and jagged peaks including Paine Grande and Fortaleza.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up the valley to the Mirador Británico or Mirador Valle del Francés for panoramic views of the hanging glaciers and surrounding peaks. Listen for the thunderous crack of calving ice from the glaciers above. Eat your packed lunch at the mirador with views of the valley below. Begin the descent back to Campamento Italiano.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the catamaran or park bus and head back toward the hotel. Arrive by 18:00–19:00. Rest and stretch tired legs. Enjoy a warm dinner at the hotel or cook in the communal kitchen.

meals.breakfast: Bread with jam and peanut butter, instant coffee — ~$2 USD
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch: wraps with cheese and salami, trail mix, energy bars — ~$5 USD
meals.dinner: Budget restaurant or self-cooked rice with canned beans and vegetables — ~$4–12 USD

day_by_day.notes: The catamaran across Lago Pehoé costs approximately $25–35 USD round trip — check current pricing and book in advance during December. Alternatively, walk the longer route around the lake to save money. The full Valle del Francés day hike is approximately 16–20km round trip with 600m elevation gain.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning. Sleep in until 08:00. Enjoy a slow breakfast. Spend the morning writing a journal, editing photos, or reading. Do light stretching or yoga to aid muscle recovery after two major hiking days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the area around Lago Grey. Take the park bus to the Grey Glacier viewpoint — a stunning blue glacier that calves icebergs into the grey-colored glacial lake. Walk the 2km viewpoint trail along the lakeshore. Look for floating icebergs in the lake and condors soaring overhead.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel by 17:30. Visit a local artisan market or small shop if available nearby. Prepare a budget dinner. Plan the second half of the trip and review remaining hikes and activities.

meals.breakfast: Scrambled eggs (if kitchen available) or cereal with powdered milk — ~$2–3 USD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Lago Grey viewpoint — crackers, hummus, dried fruit — ~$3–4 USD
meals.dinner: Self-cooked lentil soup with bread — ~$3 USD or budget restaurant ~$10–12 USD

day_by_day.notes: The Grey Glacier boat tour is available but costs ~$60–80 USD — skip to stay on budget and enjoy the free lakeshore viewpoint instead. The free walking trail to the glacier viewpoint still offers spectacular views of the ice.

day_by_day.morning: Start at 07:00. Hike the Mirador Condor trail or the Sendero Lago Grey trail — a moderate 3–4 hour hike with excellent chances of spotting Andean condors riding thermal winds above the valley. The trail offers sweeping views of the lake and surrounding mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: After returning from the morning hike, take a self-guided walk along the Río Paine river trail near the hotel. Look for Patagonian foxes, hares, and nesting birds along the riverbanks. Spend time sketching, photographing, or simply sitting and observing the wildlife.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset in December in Patagonia occurs around 22:00 — take advantage of the long daylight hours for a golden hour walk along the beachfront near the hotel. Enjoy the dramatic light on the mountains. Cook dinner and prepare gear for tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Instant oatmeal with honey and nuts — ~$2 USD
meals.lunch: Self-prepared sandwiches eaten on the trail — ~$3–4 USD
meals.dinner: Budget pasta or rice dish cooked in communal kitchen — ~$3–4 USD or local restaurant ~$10 USD

day_by_day.notes: December 21 is near the summer solstice in the Southern Hemisphere — enjoy nearly 18 hours of daylight. This is a great day to take photos during the magical golden hour light that lasts for hours in Patagonia.

day_by_day.morning: Full day hike: Sendero Pehoe to Mirador Pehoé. Start at 07:30 and hike the trail around Lago Pehoé with views of Cerro Paine Grande and the Cuernos del Paine reflected in the turquoise lake. This moderate 4–5 hour round-trip trail is less crowded than the main W Circuit routes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Mirador Los Cuernos viewpoint for dramatic close-up views of the iconic Cuernos del Paine — the horned peaks with their distinctive dark sedimentary caps over lighter granite. Eat lunch at the viewpoint and spend time photographing the landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel by 17:00. Wash and dry gear. Visit a nearby local shop or kiosk for fresh supplies. Enjoy a relaxed evening meal and early bedtime to prepare for the next day's adventure.

meals.breakfast: Bread, peanut butter, banana, instant coffee — ~$2–3 USD
meals.lunch: Trail mix, energy bars, crackers with cheese eaten at Mirador Los Cuernos — ~$4 USD
meals.dinner: Canned fish with rice and vegetables — self-cooked ~$3–4 USD or local restaurant ~$10–13 USD

day_by_day.notes: The Cuernos del Paine are best photographed in morning or late afternoon light. Bring extra layers as the wind around Lago Pehoé can be very strong — gusts of 80–100 km/h are common in Patagonia.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Puerto Natales. Take the morning shared bus (~$8–10 USD one way) to Puerto Natales for a half-day resupply and cultural exploration. Visit the Mercado Municipal for fresh local produce, empanadas, and cheap seafood. Stock up on trail food for the remaining days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Puerto Natales on foot. Visit the free Museo Histórico Municipal to learn about the history of Patagonia, the indigenous Kawésqar people, and the early European settlers. Walk along the Seno Última Esperanza waterfront for views of the fjord and distant mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sit-down budget dinner at one of Puerto Natales' affordable local restaurants before catching the late afternoon bus back to Torres del Paine. Try the local specialty — cordero al palo (spit-roasted Patagonian lamb) at a budget parilla if available within your budget.

meals.breakfast: Empanadas from the Mercado Municipal — ~$3–4 USD
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood soup (chupe de mariscos) or cazuela at a local restaurant — ~$8–10 USD
meals.dinner: Set menu at a budget restaurant in Puerto Natales — ~$10–14 USD

day_by_day.notes: Puerto Natales is the main supply hub for Torres del Paine. Use this day to restock on: energy bars, instant meals, dried fruit, nuts, sunscreen, and any trekking supplies you've run low on. The bus schedule back to the park runs until approximately 18:00 — confirm times locally.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Eve. Early morning wildlife walk starting at 07:00 near the hotel's beachfront and surrounding pampas. Guanacos are most active at dawn — look for herds grazing on the open grasslands. Bring binoculars to spot Andean condors, black-chested buzzard-eagles, and Chilean flamingos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Sendero Lago Toro trail — a relatively flat and easy 3–4 hour trail along the shores of Lago del Toro offering wide open views of the southern massif of the park. Ideal for a lighter activity day before the holiday evening.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve celebration — splurge slightly on a special budget dinner at the hotel restaurant or the nearest local eatery. Toast to the journey with a glass of Chilean carménère wine (~$3–5 USD per glass). Enjoy the long Patagonian summer evening light.

meals.breakfast: Special Christmas Eve breakfast — scrambled eggs, toast, fruit, coffee — ~$4–5 USD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the Lago Toro trail — crackers, cheese, salami, chocolate — ~$4 USD
meals.dinner: Slightly splurge: hotel restaurant or local parilla — Patagonian lamb or fresh trout — ~$18–25 USD

day_by_day.notes: Christmas is celebrated enthusiastically in Chile. The hotel may have special holiday decorations or a set Christmas Eve dinner menu — ask in advance. Budget for a small splurge tonight as a reward for your trekking achievements.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day. Slow, relaxed morning. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Spend the morning reflecting on the trip, writing postcards or journal entries, and reviewing your favorite photos from the past 10 days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final major hike of the trip: Sendero Mirador Nordenskjöld — a moderate 4–5 hour hike with spectacular views of Lago Nordenskjöld, the Cuernos del Paine, and the central massif. One of the most photogenic viewpoints in the park and less crowded on Christmas Day.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a final celebratory Christmas dinner. Treat yourself to a warm, hearty meal. Pack your bags and prepare for checkout and departure the following day. Review any remaining gear that needs to be cleaned or organized.

meals.breakfast: Special Christmas breakfast — pancakes or eggs with toast and fresh juice if available — ~$5–7 USD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Mirador Nordenskjöld — remaining trail snacks and sandwiches — ~$3–4 USD
meals.dinner: Christmas dinner at hotel restaurant — set menu or à la carte — budget ~$20–28 USD as a final splurge

day_by_day.notes: Feliz Navidad! Many services in Chile may operate on reduced hours on Christmas Day — confirm bus and shuttle schedules for December 26 departure in advance. Leave no trace: pack out all trash from your room and any remaining trail waste.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Torres del Paine. Wake up early for one last sunrise walk along the beachfront near the hotel. Take final photographs of the mountains and lake in the morning light. Enjoy a last breakfast at the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrange the pre-booked shared shuttle or bus transfer back to Puerto Natales or Punta Arenas for onward travel. During the journey, look out the window for one final view of the Torres del Paine massif as you leave the park.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Puerto Natales or Punta Arenas. If there is time before your onward flight or connection, explore the town, visit a final local restaurant for a farewell Chilean meal, or browse souvenir shops for budget-friendly local crafts and postcards.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or self-prepared — ~$3–5 USD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch for the road or bus station café — ~$4–6 USD
meals.dinner: Budget farewell dinner in Puerto Natales or Punta Arenas — cazuela or empanadas — ~$8–12 USD

day_by_day.notes: Book your return shuttle in advance — December 26 is a busy travel day in Patagonia. Shared shuttles from Torres del Paine to Puerto Natales cost approximately $15–25 USD. From Puerto Natales, buses to Punta Arenas run several times daily and cost ~$10–15 USD. Allow at least 5–6 hours of travel time between the park and Punta Arenas airport for any flights.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport via Flight UA at 22:30. Arrange pre-booked private transfer or shared shuttle to Aegean Bliss Resort in Torres del Paine. Check in, unpack, and wind down. Hydrate well and prepare gear for the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack or pre-packed meal at the airport before boarding transfer. Alternatively, ask the resort if a late-night welcome platter can be arranged upon arrival.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm transfer booking in advance. The drive from Puerto Natales to Torres del Paine typically takes 1.5–2 hours. Keep essentials (layers, headlamp, water) in carry-on for easy access upon arrival. Set alarms early for Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Slow start and resort orientation. After breakfast, take a leisurely walk around the Aegean Bliss Resort grounds and the nearby lakeshore to acclimate to the altitude and Patagonian winds. Enjoy panoramic views of the Torres massif from the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join the Patagonian Wildlife and Pampas Nature Walk around Lago Sarmiento and Laguna Amarga. This gentle 3–4 hour guided walk introduces you to the open steppe ecosystem. Spot guanacos, ñandus (rheas), Andean condors, and flamingos in their natural habitat — perfect for easing into the park without overexertion.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by late afternoon. Shower and rest. Head to the resort restaurant or a nearby mid-range eatery for a relaxed dinner. Review maps and gear for upcoming treks.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — eggs, fresh bread, local cheeses, coffee, and fruit.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or light snacks brought on the nature walk — sandwiches, trail mix, fruit, and thermos of hot tea.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant or El Asador Patagónico-style grill nearby — lamb stew or grilled salmon with local vegetables and a glass of Chilean Carménère.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase or confirm your Torres del Paine National Park entrance pass today if not done online. Entrance fees are required. Laguna Amarga is a common flamingo hotspot — bring binoculars. Wind can be fierce even on calm days; always carry a windproof jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike. Depart resort by 05:00 to reach the trailhead at Hostería Las Torres. Begin the 8-hour round-trip hike ascending through lenga beech forest and a steep glacial moraine to reach the iconic granite towers at sunrise. The golden light on the towers is a once-in-a-lifetime sight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying the mirador at the base of the towers before beginning the descent. Take your time on the moraine — the footing is uneven. Arrive back at the trailhead by early-to-mid afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer back to Aegean Bliss Resort. Soak tired legs, stretch, and rest. Enjoy a hearty dinner at the resort to replenish energy after the strenuous hike.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure — oatmeal, banana, coffee, and energy bars to go.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the mirador — sandwiches, hard-boiled eggs, nuts, chocolate, and plenty of water.
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at the resort restaurant — hearty Patagonian lamb (cordero al palo) or pasta, soup starter, and dessert.

day_by_day.notes: This is the most physically demanding day of the trip. Wear layered clothing — temperatures at the top can be 10–15°C colder than the base. Trekking poles are highly recommended for the moraine section. Carry at least 2 liters of water and high-calorie snacks. Check weather forecast the night before — if conditions are severe, consider rescheduling.

day_by_day.morning: Active recovery day. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Take a short, flat walk along the lakeshore near the resort to keep muscles moving without overloading them. Enjoy the scenery and photograph the changing Patagonian light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the park's visitor center or ranger station to learn about the park's geology, ecology, and conservation efforts. Browse any local artisan stalls or small shops in the nearby area. Alternatively, arrange a short horseback riding session (available through some local operators near the park) for a different perspective of the pampas.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort. Enjoy a sunset from the resort's viewpoint or lakeside area — December sunsets in Patagonia can last until 22:00 or later. Light dinner and early bed to prepare for multi-day trekking.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — pancakes, local honey, fresh juice, yogurt, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at the resort café or a nearby refugio — empanadas, soup, and fresh bread.
meals.dinner: Light but nutritious dinner — grilled trout with quinoa salad, vegetable soup, and herbal tea.

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to repack your backpack for the W Trek starting tomorrow. Separate items you won't need and leave them securely at the resort. Charge all electronics, fill water bottles, and confirm refugio or camping bookings along the W Trek route. Pack a 3-day supply of snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the W Trek — Day 1. Depart resort early and transfer to the Paine Grande refugio (western starting point). Start trekking toward the Grey Glacier viewpoint. The trail winds through open terrain with stunning views of Lago Grey and the glacier's blue ice face. Distance: approximately 11 km one-way to Refugio Grey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking along Lago Grey, passing viewpoints with floating icebergs. Arrive at Refugio Grey by mid-afternoon. Check in to your pre-booked refugio bed (mid-range option with dorm or semi-private room). Rest and explore the glacier viewpoints near the refugio.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the glacier glow in the long Patagonian evening light from the refugio deck. Socialize with fellow trekkers from around the world. Prepare gear for the next day.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail — energy bars, dried fruit, crackers with peanut butter, and water.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Refugio Grey — set menu typically includes soup, a main course (pasta or meat), and dessert. Included or available for purchase at the refugio (~$25–35 USD).

day_by_day.notes: W Trek bookings (refugios and/or campsites) must be made well in advance through CONAF or Vertice Patagonia/Las Torres operators. Carry a 45–60L pack with sleeping bag liner, rain gear, warm layers, and 3 days of snacks. The trail can be very windy — secure all loose items on your pack.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek — Day 2. Wake early at Refugio Grey. After breakfast, join the Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition as an optional add-on from the refugio (pre-book in advance). Paddle through iceberg-dotted Lago Grey waters alongside the massive glacier face — an extraordinary and intimate perspective of the ice.
day_by_day.afternoon: After kayaking, begin trekking back east from Refugio Grey toward Paine Grande refugio (approximately 11 km). The return trail offers different angles of the glacier and the Paine massif. Arrive at Paine Grande by mid-afternoon and check in.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at Paine Grande refugio. Enjoy the communal atmosphere. Review tomorrow's route to Valle del Francés. Sunset views over Lago Pehoé from the refugio are spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Refugio Grey breakfast — oatmeal, bread, jam, coffee, and juice.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail or a light snack at Paine Grande refugio café.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Paine Grande refugio — set menu with soup, main, and dessert.

day_by_day.notes: The kayaking expedition typically runs 2–3 hours and requires pre-booking. Dry bags are provided but bring a change of dry clothes. After kayaking, the return trek is moderately demanding — pace yourself. Paine Grande is a larger hub with better facilities than Grey refugio.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek — Day 3: Valle del Francés Trekking Day. Depart Paine Grande early. Trek northeast toward Campamento Italiano at the entrance of Valle del Francés. Drop your large pack at the campamento and begin the ascent into the valley with a daypack. The valley is flanked by hanging glaciers, dramatic cliff faces, and the Paine Grande peak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue ascending to Mirador Británico (the highest viewpoint in the valley) for panoramic views of the French Valley, glaciers, and the Cuernos del Paine. Descend back to Campamento Italiano, collect your pack, and continue trekking east to Refugio Los Cuernos. Arrive by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Refugio Los Cuernos — one of the most scenic refugios in the park, set directly below the iconic Cuernos peaks. Enjoy the dramatic evening light on the Cuernos. Rest and prepare for the final W Trek leg tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Paine Grande before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten in Valle del Francés — ideally at the Mirador Británico with one of the best views in Patagonia.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Refugio Los Cuernos — set menu with local-inspired dishes.

day_by_day.notes: This is the most scenically rewarding day of the W Trek. The round-trip into Valle del Francés adds approximately 8–10 km to the day's total, making it a long day (20+ km total). Start early. Listen for the thunderous crack of calving glaciers echoing through the valley — an unforgettable natural sound.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek — Day 4 (Final Leg). Depart Refugio Los Cuernos and trek east along the northern shore of Lago Nordenskjöld toward Hostería Las Torres. The trail passes through beautiful lenga beech forest with views of the Cuernos and the lake. Distance: approximately 11 km.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Hostería Las Torres area by midday. Freshen up and enjoy lunch at the hostería restaurant — a well-deserved treat after 4 days on trail. Arrange transfer back to Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrive at the resort by mid-to-late afternoon. Shower, do laundry, and decompress.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate completing the W Trek with a proper dinner at the resort restaurant. Reflect on the journey, review photos, and enjoy a full bed and warm shower.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Refugio Los Cuernos before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Hostería Las Torres restaurant — burger, salad, or pasta with a cold drink. Budget ~$20–30 USD.
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — three-course meal with Chilean wine. Treat yourself — you've earned it.

day_by_day.notes: Post-trek, check your feet for blisters and treat them promptly. Rehydrate thoroughly. Leave boots outside to air out. Back at the resort, request a laundry service if available to clean trekking clothes. Rest is the priority this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery day. Sleep in as long as needed. Enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast at the resort. Spend the morning reading, journaling, or simply sitting by the water and watching the ever-changing Patagonian sky and wildlife.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional light activity: take a short, flat nature walk near the resort along the lakeshore. Look for Patagonian foxes, hares, and birds of prey. Alternatively, book a massage or spa treatment at the resort if available. Visit any small local crafts market or shop in the area to pick up souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset photography session from the resort grounds — December evenings offer extraordinary golden-hour light lasting until 22:00+. Enjoy a relaxed dinner with a focus on local Patagonian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent late breakfast at the resort — eggs benedict, fresh pastries, fruit platter, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort café — avocado toast, soup, or a fresh salad.
meals.dinner: Mid-range dinner at the resort or a nearby local restaurant — Patagonian king crab (centolla) if available, with local bread and Chilean white wine.

day_by_day.notes: Your body needs recovery after the W Trek. Don't underestimate the physical toll — rest is as important as activity. Use this day to organize photos, write postcards, and plan any last-minute activities for the remaining days.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to explore a different section of the park. Head to the Laguna Azul area in the northeastern part of Torres del Paine for a quieter, less-crowded trekking experience. The trail around Laguna Azul offers beautiful reflections of the Torres and abundant wildlife on the open pampas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the northeastern sector. Visit Laguna Verde if accessible, another stunning turquoise lake with a different color palette caused by algae and mineral content. Picnic lunch with views of the lake and surrounding steppe.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Tonight is Christmas Eve — enjoy a special festive dinner at the resort. Many Patagonian lodges and restaurants offer a special holiday menu. Toast to an incredible journey in one of the world's most remote and beautiful places.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch at Laguna Verde or Laguna Azul — local cheeses, cured meats, bread, fruit, and sparkling water.
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — festive set menu with traditional Chilean and Patagonian dishes, wine pairing, and dessert. Budget ~$40–60 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Laguna Azul is in the lesser-visited northeastern sector of the park — you'll likely encounter far fewer tourists here. Bring binoculars for excellent guanaco and condor spotting. Check if the resort has any special Christmas Eve events or activities planned.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas morning at one of the most spectacular places on Earth. Wake up early and watch the sunrise over the Torres del Paine massif from the resort grounds — a truly magical Christmas gift. Enjoy a leisurely festive breakfast at the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a half-day guided boat tour on Lago Pehoé or Lago Grey (bookable through the resort or local operators). These boat excursions offer unique perspectives of the park's lakes, glaciers, and peaks that are impossible to see from land. Return to resort by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Torres del Paine. Spend time reflecting on the journey, organizing photos, and packing. Enjoy a memorable Christmas dinner at the resort with fellow travelers. Share stories, make toasts, and soak in the last hours of this extraordinary destination.

meals.breakfast: Festive Christmas breakfast at the resort — special holiday spread with champagne or sparkling juice, fresh pastries, smoked salmon, and hot drinks.
meals.lunch: Light lunch on the boat or back at the resort café after the tour.
meals.dinner: Christmas dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — special holiday menu featuring traditional Patagonian cordero (lamb), seasonal sides, and a festive dessert with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Some boat tours may have reduced schedules on Christmas Day — confirm bookings in advance. This is a day to be fully present and grateful. Tip your resort staff generously — they're working on a holiday to make your experience special. Begin packing tonight to ease tomorrow's departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Torres del Paine. Wake up early for one last sunrise walk near the resort. Take final photos and breathe in the crisp Patagonian air. Enjoy a full resort breakfast. Complete packing and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange transfer from the resort to Puerto Natales or Punta Arenas depending on your onward flight. Use travel time to reflect on the journey. If time permits before your flight, explore Puerto Natales briefly — visit the waterfront, browse the artisan market on the main plaza, or stop at a local café for one last Patagonian coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Punta Arenas airport. Carry memories of the Torres del Paine granite towers, the Grey Glacier's blue ice, the Valle del Francés hanging glaciers, and the endless Patagonian sky.

meals.breakfast: Final full breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — make it count.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Puerto Natales if time allows — La Mesita Grande for pizza, or Afrigonia for a creative local-international fusion meal. Budget ~$15–25 USD.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal — pack some local snacks (dried fruits, chocolate, Patagonian cookies) for the journey home.

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample travel time — the drive from Torres del Paine to Punta Arenas airport is approximately 3–4 hours. Book your transfer in advance and confirm the night before. Declare any food items at customs. Keep souvenirs, trekking permits, and park maps as keepsakes. Consider writing a review for the resort and experiences to help future travelers.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Torres del Paine, Patagonia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Torres del Paine, Patagonia

experiences.name: W Trek Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic W Trek, a 4-5 day trekking route through Torres del Paine National Park covering the Valle del Francés, Grey Glacier, and the iconic Torres viewpoint. Experience dramatic landscapes of granite towers, turquoise lakes, and Patagonian steppe with overnight stays in mountain refugios or campsites.
experiences.location: Torres del Paine National Park, Central Circuit

experiences.name: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Trek the challenging 8-hour round-trip trail to the base of the iconic Torres del Paine granite towers. Start before dawn to witness the legendary alpenglow phenomenon where the towers glow fiery orange and pink at sunrise, reflecting in the glacial lake below. One of Patagonia's most breathtaking natural spectacles.
experiences.location: Mirador Base Las Torres, Eastern Sector

experiences.name: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition
experiences.description: Paddle through iceberg-dotted waters of Lago Grey alongside the massive Grey Glacier, one of Patagonia's most accessible glaciers. A guided kayaking experience allows you to get up close to towering blue ice walls and floating icebergs while surrounded by the raw wilderness of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field.

experiences.name: Valle del Francés Trekking Day
experiences.description: Hike through the spectacular Valle del Francés, a glacially carved valley flanked by hanging glaciers, waterfalls, and the dramatic Cuernos del Paine peaks. Ascend to the Mirador Británico viewpoint for a 360-degree panorama of the park's most stunning peaks and valleys. Watch for condors soaring overhead.

experiences.name: Patagonian Wildlife and Pampas Nature Walk
experiences.description: Explore the open Patagonian steppe and lakeside trails around Lago Sarmiento and Laguna Amarga to spot abundant wildlife including guanacos, rheas, Andean condors, flamingos, and pumas in their natural habitat. A guided nature walk reveals the unique flora and fauna of the Patagonian ecosystem beyond the main trekking routes.
experiences.location: Laguna Amarga and Lago Sarmiento, Northern Entrance Sector

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Private luxury transfer arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort awaits at arrivals. Scenic 5-hour drive (or optional chartered flight connection) to Torres del Paine area. Enjoy a welcome hamper of Patagonian wines, artisan cheeses, and charcuterie in your private vehicle.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Welcome hamper served in private transfer vehicle — curated selection of Carménère and Sauvignon Blanc from Concha y Toro's premium range, smoked Patagonian lamb, aged cheeses, and artisan crackers

day_by_day.notes: Late arrival — check-in at Aegean Bliss Resort is pre-arranged for after midnight. Resort staff will be on hand to welcome guests regardless of arrival time. Luggage handling and unpacking service available. No alarm needed for Day 2 morning — a leisurely start is recommended to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a slow, restorative morning. Take a private sunrise stroll along the beachfront of the resort as the first light illuminates the Paine Massif across the lake. Indulge in a full gourmet breakfast at the resort's panoramic dining room overlooking the water. Meet your dedicated personal guide for a private orientation briefing covering the 12-day itinerary, gear check, and safety protocols.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on a gentle introductory nature walk — the Patagonian Wildlife and Pampas Nature Walk around Lago Sarmiento and Laguna Amarga. This easy-to-moderate 3–4 hour walk is perfect for acclimatization and jet-lag recovery. Spot guanacos, flamingos, ñandús (rheas), Andean condors, and foxes against the sweeping steppe landscape. Your private naturalist guide provides expert wildlife commentary throughout.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a private hot tub session and optional in-room massage (pre-bookable with the concierge). Enjoy a welcome dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant featuring a curated tasting menu of Patagonian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet Patagonian breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — freshly baked medialunas, smoked salmon, local berry preserves, farm eggs cooked to order, fresh fruit platters, and barista-crafted coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic hamper served lakeside during the nature walk — smoked trout, quinoa salad, empanadas, seasonal fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Welcome tasting menu at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant — 6-course dinner featuring Patagonian lamb, king crab, native mushroom risotto, and local berry dessert, paired with a curated Chilean wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Gear and trekking equipment check with your guide today. The resort's boutique outfitter can supply or upgrade any missing items. Weather conditions in Torres del Paine are highly variable — always carry wind and waterproof layers. Sunscreen and UV-protection sunglasses are essential even on overcast days.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (06:00) by private 4x4 vehicle into Torres del Paine National Park for the iconic Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike. Begin the trail from the Hotel Las Torres trailhead, ascending through lenga beech forests and dramatic moraine fields. The 8-hour round-trip hike (approximately 19 km) reaches the turquoise glacial lake at the base of the three granite towers — one of Patagonia's most breathtaking vistas. Your private guide leads at a comfortable pace with expert geological and ecological commentary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach the mirador (viewpoint) at the base of the towers by midday, enjoying the spectacular light on the granite spires. Enjoy a gourmet packed lunch at the summit area. Begin the descent through the same dramatic terrain, with time to pause at viewpoints and photograph condors soaring overhead.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by 17:00–18:00. Enjoy a restorative soak in the outdoor heated pool or private hot tub overlooking the lake. Wind down with a Pisco Sour at the resort bar before a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-hike breakfast at 05:30 — high-energy options including porridge, eggs, avocado toast, fresh juice, and coffee prepared by the resort kitchen
meals.lunch: Gourmet summit picnic hamper — Patagonian lamb sandwiches on artisan bread, energy bars, dried fruit, nuts, thermos of hot soup, and herbal tea
meals.dinner: À la carte dinner at the resort — grilled Patagonian centolla (king crab) with lemon butter, followed by slow-roasted lamb shoulder with native herbs and Andean potato gratin, with a premium Malbec selection

day_by_day.notes: This is one of the most physically demanding days of the itinerary — 8 hours of hiking with significant elevation gain. Trekking poles strongly recommended. Depart early to secure the best light and avoid afternoon winds. Weather on the towers can change rapidly — waterproof layers and warm mid-layers are mandatory. The private guide carries a first-aid kit and satellite communicator.

day_by_day.morning: Active recovery morning — optional gentle yoga session on the resort's outdoor deck with panoramic mountain views, led by the resort's wellness instructor. Follow with a leisurely breakfast and a private briefing from your guide on the upcoming W Trek multi-day adventure. Spend time reviewing maps, packing strategy, and gear optimization with your guide and the resort's expedition team.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon excursion to explore the shores of Lago del Toro near the resort. Private kayaking session on calm resort-area waters as a warm-up for the Grey Glacier kayaking experience later in the trip. Alternatively, explore the resort's private trail network through native lenga beech forest with your naturalist guide, discovering Patagonian flora and birdlife up close.
day_by_day.evening: Private stargazing experience on the resort terrace with a resident astronomer guide — Torres del Paine's remote location offers extraordinary dark skies in the austral summer. Enjoy hot chocolate and Patagonian spirits under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed late breakfast — smashed avocado on sourdough, poached eggs, smoked Patagonian trout, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Casual lakeside lunch at the resort's terrace bistro — grilled vegetable flatbreads, fresh ceviche, and house-made lemonade
meals.dinner: Chef's table experience at the resort — intimate 8-course degustation dinner with the executive chef presenting each dish personally, featuring hyper-local Patagonian ingredients and paired with premium Chilean and Argentine wines

day_by_day.notes: Today is intentionally lighter to allow recovery from Day 3's demanding hike and preparation for the upcoming W Trek multi-day adventure starting tomorrow. The resort's concierge will arrange all W Trek logistics, including porter service, premium refugio upgrades, and private guide coordination. Luggage storage at the resort is available for non-essential items during the trek.

day_by_day.morning: Depart at 07:00 for the start of the W Trek Multi-Day Hike — Day 1 of the iconic route. Begin at the eastern arm of the W at Laguna Amarga, transferring by private catamaran across Lago Nordenskjöld to Paine Grande. Trek the first segment toward the Valle del Francés camp, ascending through open steppe and transitional forest with sweeping views of the lake and Cuernos del Paine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking into the Valle del Francés — a glacially carved valley flanked by hanging glaciers, dramatic waterfalls, and towering granite walls. Ascend to the Mirador Británico viewpoint for panoramic 360-degree views of the massif, hanging glaciers calving ice, and the valley below. This afternoon section is the Valle del Francés Trekking Day experience in full — approximately 6–7 hours of trekking for the full day.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at premium refugio accommodation (pre-booked private room upgrade) in the Valle del Francés area. Enjoy a hot shower, hearty refugio dinner, and early rest in preparation for tomorrow's continuation.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast before departure — full hot breakfast with eggs, meats, pastries, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch prepared by the resort kitchen and carried in your daypack — artisan sandwiches, energy balls, fresh fruit, and a thermos of hot soup
meals.dinner: Premium refugio dinner — three-course meal with wine, featuring the refugio's best options (typically hearty pasta, grilled meats, and dessert)

day_by_day.notes: This marks the start of the 4-day W Trek segment. A private porter service carries the majority of your luggage between refugios, allowing you to hike with a light daypack. Your private guide accompanies the group throughout all W Trek days. Premium refugio rooms are pre-booked with private or semi-private configurations. All meals during the W Trek are pre-arranged and pre-paid.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 2 — Early morning departure from Valle del Francés refugio. Trek westward along the southern arm of the W toward Paine Grande and the Grey Glacier sector. The trail passes through native forest, open pampas, and offers continuous views of Lago Grey and the surrounding peaks. Approximately 4–5 hours of trekking to reach the Grey sector.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Lago Grey and embark on the Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition — paddle through the iceberg-dotted turquoise waters of Lago Grey alongside the massive face of Grey Glacier, one of Patagonia's most impressive ice fields. Your private kayaking guide provides expert instruction and narrates the glaciological significance of the ice field. This 3–4 hour paddling experience is a highlight of the entire trip.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to premium refugio accommodation at Grey sector. Dry off, warm up by the refugio fire, and enjoy a well-earned dinner with fellow trekkers and your guide. Toast the day's achievements with a glass of Chilean wine.

meals.breakfast: Hot refugio breakfast — porridge, eggs, toast, fresh coffee, and juice
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch consumed at a scenic viewpoint along the trek — premium sandwiches, snacks, and hot thermos
meals.dinner: Refugio dinner with wine — hearty three-course meal featuring warming soups, grilled protein, and dessert

day_by_day.notes: The Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition requires participants to wear dry suits and life vests provided by the operator. No prior kayaking experience is necessary. Water temperatures are near freezing — the dry suits ensure comfort and safety. This is one of the most exclusive experiences on the itinerary and is weather-dependent; your guide will confirm viability on the morning of the activity.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 3 — Optional early morning walk to the Grey Glacier viewpoint platform for sunrise views of the glacier and floating icebergs before breakfast. Begin the return trek eastward along the northern arm of the W, retracing partially through the Grey sector and heading toward the central camp at Paine Grande. The morning section offers dramatic views of the ice field and Lago Pehoé.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking through the central section of the W, passing through wildflower meadows and lenga beech forest. Arrive at Paine Grande camp by early afternoon. Optional short side hike to a nearby viewpoint for photographs of the Cuernos del Paine reflected in the lake. Rest and recovery time at the refugio before dinner.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at Paine Grande refugio. Engage in a guided photography workshop with your guide — capturing the golden hour light on the Cuernos del Paine and lake reflections. Share stories and highlights from the trek over dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hot refugio breakfast — eggs, toast, porridge, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch at a lakeside rest stop — premium wraps, energy bars, dried fruit, and hot soup
meals.dinner: Paine Grande refugio dinner — three-course meal with a celebratory bottle of Carménère to mark the halfway point of the W Trek

day_by_day.notes: Today is a moderate trekking day allowing for recovery and enjoyment of the scenery at a relaxed pace. Photography conditions in the afternoon and evening light are exceptional in this area — ensure camera batteries are fully charged. The private guide will assist with composition and timing for the best shots.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 4 — Final day of the W Trek. Depart Paine Grande early by private catamaran across Lago Pehoé, skipping the redundant eastward trail section to maximize time. Transfer by private vehicle to the eastern arm of the W at Hotel Las Torres. Begin the final ascent back toward Mirador Las Torres — this time approaching from a different angle and in different light conditions for a completely new perspective.
day_by_day.afternoon: Complete the final section of the W Trek, arriving at the base of the Torres del Paine towers for the second time — a triumphant conclusion to the multi-day adventure. Spend unhurried time at the mirador, reflecting on the journey and capturing final photographs. Descend at a relaxed pace through the moraine and lenga beech forest.
day_by_day.evening: Private vehicle transfer back to Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrive to a hero's welcome — the resort has prepared a recovery suite with hot bath drawn with Patagonian herbal salts, a chilled bottle of Champagne, and a personalized congratulatory note from the resort manager. Enjoy a celebratory dinner at the resort's finest table.

meals.breakfast: Final W Trek refugio breakfast — full hot breakfast with all available options
meals.lunch: Gourmet celebratory picnic at the base of the Torres — the resort's kitchen has prepared a special hamper delivered by the guide, including smoked meats, fine cheeses, sparkling wine, and artisan chocolates
meals.dinner: W Trek completion celebration dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — premium 7-course tasting menu with Champagne toast, featuring the resort's finest dishes and a personalized menu card as a keepsake

day_by_day.notes: The completion of the W Trek is a significant achievement — approximately 70–80 km of trekking over 4 days. The resort has been notified in advance to prepare the recovery suite and celebration arrangements. Trekking gear will be cleaned and dried by resort staff overnight. A deep-tissue sports massage is recommended and can be booked for the evening or the following morning.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery morning. Sleep as late as desired. Enjoy breakfast in bed with panoramic mountain views. Book a 90-minute deep-tissue sports massage at the resort spa, specifically designed for post-trekking muscle recovery. Alternatively, enjoy a float session in the resort's heated outdoor pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely afternoon exploring the resort's private grounds and beachfront. Optional guided fly-fishing excursion on a nearby Patagonian river — the region's pristine glacial rivers are world-renowned for wild rainbow and brown trout. A private fishing guide provides all equipment, instruction, and licenses. Catch-and-release philosophy maintained throughout.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour on the resort's waterfront terrace — enjoy a curated selection of Patagonian craft spirits, pisco cocktails, and Chilean wines as the alpenglow turns the Paine Massif golden. Pre-Christmas festive decorations and atmosphere at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in bed — full gourmet tray service with fresh-squeezed juice, pastries, eggs, smoked salmon, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Relaxed terrace lunch at the resort — fresh ceviche, grilled fish tacos, craft beer, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Festive pre-Christmas dinner at the resort — special seasonal menu featuring roasted Patagonian lamb, native berry sauces, and traditional Chilean holiday desserts, with live acoustic guitar music

day_by_day.notes: This is a designated rest day — no strenuous activities are planned. Guests are encouraged to sleep in, use spa facilities, and recharge. The resort concierge is available to arrange any additional experiences or special requests. Fly-fishing excursion is optional and weather-dependent.

day_by_day.morning: Morning horseback riding excursion through the Patagonian steppe with a private gaucho guide — explore the open pampas surrounding the resort on criollo horses, experiencing the landscape from a traditional Patagonian perspective. The 3-hour ride passes through areas frequented by guanacos and condors, with stunning views of the massif.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a relaxed afternoon. Visit the resort's private photography gallery showcasing Patagonian landscapes, or enjoy a curated nature documentary screening in the resort's private cinema room. Late afternoon wildlife spotting walk along the resort's beachfront with the naturalist guide — flamingos and black-necked swans are frequently seen at this time of day.
day_by_day.evening: Special Christmas Eve Gala Dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — a festive celebration featuring a lavish multi-course feast, live music, Champagne, and a warm Patagonian holiday atmosphere. The resort's team creates an unforgettable evening under the summer solstice sky of the southern hemisphere.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast before the riding excursion — high-energy options with eggs, meats, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Post-ride asado (traditional Patagonian barbecue) lunch at the resort — slow-roasted lamb and beef cooked over open fire by the resort's gaucho chef, with chimichurri, fresh salads, and red wine
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve Gala Dinner — 8-course festive tasting menu with Champagne welcome, featuring king crab, Patagonian lamb, truffle risotto, and a spectacular dessert table, with live music and dancing

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of the most special evenings of the trip. The resort creates a magical atmosphere with festive decorations, bonfires on the beachfront, and personalized gifts for guests. Smart casual attire is recommended for the Gala Dinner. The horseback riding excursion requires no prior experience — horses are matched to rider ability.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas morning sunrise hike — a private guided walk to a nearby elevated viewpoint to watch the Christmas Day sunrise illuminate the Torres del Paine massif in shades of gold and pink. A thermos of hot chocolate and a small gift from the resort await at the summit. Return for a special Christmas breakfast celebration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private full-day nature and wildlife immersion experience — your naturalist guide leads a comprehensive exploration of the park's diverse ecosystems, from the Patagonian steppe to lakeside wetlands. Focus on photography, birdwatching, and wildlife tracking. Visit Laguna Amarga for flamingo and guanaco sightings. This is a relaxed, unhurried experience celebrating the natural wonder of Patagonia on Christmas Day.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Day farewell dinner — as the penultimate evening of the trip, the resort pulls out all the stops for a magnificent celebration of the journey. Private dining setup on the beachfront terrace under the stars, with personalized service, a curated wine pairing, and a special gift from the Aegean Bliss Resort team.

meals.breakfast: Special Christmas breakfast at the resort — festive spread with Champagne, smoked salmon, eggs Benedict, pastries, tropical fruits, and all the trimmings
meals.lunch: Christmas picnic in the park — the resort prepares a luxurious hamper with cold cuts, artisan cheeses, pâtés, fresh bread, and a bottle of premium Sauvignon Blanc
meals.dinner: Private beachfront Christmas dinner — 7-course celebration menu with personalized menu cards, featuring the best of Patagonian cuisine, paired with a vertical tasting of premium Chilean wines, ending with a traditional Patagonian dessert and digestif

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day in Patagonia is a truly unique experience — the austral summer means long daylight hours (up to 17+ hours of light), making for spectacular evening light on the mountains. The resort team works through the holiday to ensure guests have an extraordinary experience. A heartfelt thank-you note to the resort team and guide is a thoughtful gesture.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Torres del Paine. Wake early for one last sunrise from the resort's beachfront — savoring the view of the Paine Massif that has been the backdrop to 12 extraordinary days. Enjoy a leisurely farewell breakfast at the resort. Pack and check out with full concierge assistance — the resort team handles all luggage and logistics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer departs the resort for Punta Arenas Airport (or Puerto Natales for connecting transport). The journey allows for one final stop at a scenic viewpoint to photograph the Torres del Paine from the road — a last farewell to one of the world's most spectacular landscapes. Transfer time approximately 4–5 hours to Punta Arenas.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas in time for onward flights. If departure is late evening, the resort's concierge pre-arranges a private day room at a luxury Punta Arenas hotel (Hotel José Nogueira or similar) for freshening up, a farewell dinner, and comfortable waiting before the flight.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — the full gourmet spread, enjoyed slowly and savored as a final memory of the resort
meals.lunch: Gourmet transfer hamper provided by the resort for the journey — artisan sandwiches, Patagonian chocolates, local biscuits, sparkling water, and a small bottle of premium Chilean wine as a parting gift
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at La Marmita or Santolla restaurant in Punta Arenas (if timing allows) — Patagonian king crab (centolla) is the must-order dish, paired with a crisp Chilean white wine as a final taste of the region

day_by_day.notes: The resort concierge will confirm all departure logistics 48 hours in advance, including transfer timing, flight check-in requirements, and any last-minute arrangements. A personalized memory book of the trip, compiled by the resort's photography team from images shared during the stay, may be presented as a farewell gift. Ensure all trekking gear, permits, and personal items are accounted for before departure. The W Trek completion certificate (if applicable) will be presented by the guide on the final morning.
